sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Genesis and Objective**: Originally conceptualized in 2009 under the UPA government to overhaul the **Income Tax Act, 1961**, transitioning towards a modern, simple, and stable tax regime.
• **Core Pillars**: Focus on lower tax rates, wider tax base, elimination of distortionary exemptions, and minimization of **tax litigation** through codified certainty.
• **Akhilesh Ranjan Task Force (2019)**: Re-evaluated the DTC framework under the Modi administration, recommending a complete overhaul of corporate and personal income tax structures.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Direct tax-to-GDP ratio improvement and reduction of effective tax exemptions (tax expenditures) that historically plagued revenue collections.

items.definition: EET means contributions and accumulations are tax-free, but withdrawals are taxed. EEE allows complete tax exemption at all three stages. DTC initially proposed moving several instruments to EET to plug revenue leakages.

items.term: Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) / Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT)
items.definition: Mechanisms historically used to tax zero-tax companies and corporate dividend payouts; DTC aimed to rationalize or replace them to improve investment sentiment.
An anti-tax avoidance framework initially rooted in the DTC proposals, empowering tax authorities to declare arrangements as 'impermissible avoidance arrangements'.
Kelkar Task Force on Direct Taxes (2002), Vijay Kelkar Committee, and Akhilesh Ranjan Task Force (2019) laid the conceptual groundwork for the Direct Taxes Code.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Institutional Hubs
items.content:
• **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)**: Statutory body under the Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963, responsible for framing direct tax policies in New Delhi.
• **National e-Assessment Centre (NeAC)**: Decentralized digital hubs across major metros (Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru) implementing faceless assessment regimens aligned with DTC philosophy.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Revenue foregone due to exemptions, prolonged judicial litigation in High Courts/Supreme Court, and friction between taxpayers and tax administration.
• **Policy Interventions**: Shift toward Faceless Assessment, Vivad se Vishwas Scheme, corporate tax rate cuts (2019), and gradual adoption of codified principles rather than a single massive DTC enactment.

items.title: Mnemonic for Tax Savings Systems (EEE vs EET)
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: "Enter Free, Grow Free, Take Taxed" (EF-GF-TT).
• **Decoded Meaning**: E-E-T means Exempt (contribution), Exempt (accrual), Taxed (withdrawal).
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly distinguishes EET from traditional EEE schemes like PPF.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: DTC = Less Exemptions + Lower Rates + Broader Base + Zero Litigation.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently poses statements claiming that the Direct Taxes Code (DTC) completely replaced the Income Tax Act of 1961. Remember, despite multiple committees and draft bills, a comprehensive standalone DTC has not replaced the 1961 Act; rather, its principles have been selectively incorporated via annual Finance Acts and corporate tax cuts.

Mains Value Addition: In answers regarding tax reforms, quote the Economic Survey recommendation on 'Enabling a Legal Framework for Transparency' and mention how moving from discretionary exemptions to a codified rule-based system enhances India's Tax-to-GDP ratio.

keyTakeaways: The Direct Taxes Code (DTC) was conceptualized to replace the 1961 Income Tax Act with a simpler, modern, and exemption-free tax regime.
Key elements of DTC evolution include moving towards anti-avoidance rules (GAAR), rationalizing tax slabs, and lowering corporate tax burdens.
While a formal standalone DTC enactment remains pending, its core tenets heavily influence ongoing Indian tax administrative reforms like faceless assessment and dispute resolution.
